title: Modes: why vim is different
summary: Normal, insert, visual and command-line mode, and the keys that move between them.

steps.title: Keys are commands
body: In nano every key you type goes into the file. In vim, when the file opens you are in **normal mode**: keys are **commands**. `x` deletes a character, `dd` deletes a line, `u` undoes. This is the whole trick of vim: editing is something you *say*, not something you drag.
There are four modes you need:
| Mode | You get there with | Keys mean | Bottom line shows |
| **Insert** | `i`, `a`, `o` and friends | text to type | `-- INSERT --` |
| **Command-line** | `:` (also `/`, `?`) | an Ex command, run with Enter | `:` and what you type |
**Esc always takes you back to normal mode.** When in doubt, press Esc (twice does no harm).
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: You open a file in vim and immediately type `hello`. What happens?
options: vim runs commands: `h` moves left, `e` jumps to a word end, `l` moves right, `l` again, `o` opens a new line below and enters insert mode
vim shows an error and quits
steps.explain: Normal mode treats every key as a command. Only after `o` are you in insert mode. This is why new users see strange things happen.

steps.title: Getting into insert mode
body: Each way in puts the cursor somewhere different:
| `I` | at the first non-blank of the line |
| `A` | at the end of the line |
Type your text, then `Esc` to get back to normal mode. A habit worth building: **every edit ends with Esc**.

steps.prompt: The line is `port 80` and the cursor is on the `p`. You press `A`, type `80`, press `Esc`. What is the line now?
steps.explain: `A` appends at the very end of the line, wherever the cursor was.

steps.prompt: The file is one line, `server {`, with the cursor on `s`. You press `o`, type `    listen 443;` (four spaces first), press `Esc`. What does the file contain?
steps.explain: `o` opens a new line below and enters insert mode.

steps.title: Real keys: type, save, quit
prompt: Now in a Vim emulator that reacts to every key like Vim. Add `hello` before ` world`, then save and quit with one command.
Watch the bottom line: `-- INSERT --` while you type, empty again after `Esc`. Then try **Get me out of here** and **Throw it away** in the same trainer.
steps.explain: `i` to type, `Esc` to stop typing, `:wq` Enter to write and quit. Eleven keys, and you can leave any Vim on any server.
